title: The Last Defense
subtitle: They take to the saddle because this land raised them.

trails.title: After the Shots
trails.description: The chief of staff has never looked this troubled. She even forgot to remove her spurs when she entered the room.

content.text: Their masters remain quiet ... for the most part. And you know why.
So the masters whistle. Just a pitch. No words.
And so, no words are heard—only the baying of dogs.
What do you mean, "I know why"?

branch.text: Perhaps you've forgotten the words echoed in that cave ... darling. Never mind.
Forgetfulness can be a mercy. Especially in this dog fight.
If only these hounds would forget their training ... then perhaps, at last, the barking would stop.
How dare you! To think I should speak like some slick-talking veteran!
I'd slit my throat myself if I so much as uttered a word akin to those devils!
They're bastards—abominations! Every last one of them! I—
Ahem ... Please accept my apologies. Wounds are hard to heal when they are torn open time and time again.

content.text: You sound like a soldier I know.

items.text: The Last Defense

items.speaker: Levchuk
items.text: Good to hear your voice, Admiral!

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: Is that Levchuk? You're still alive?

items.speaker: Levchuk
items.text: This is urgent. Enemy forces are marching toward the southern bank. Their armored convoy has already reached Tamarovka!

items.speaker: Levchuk
items.text: There are at least two armored divisions and one infantry division, plus three artillery regiments!

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Roger. Good work.
The man on the other end collapses to the floor with relief.
The gunfire in the background sharpens. Igor hopes it's just his mind playing tricks on him.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Report your position, Staff Sergeant. A squad will be sent to your rescue immediately.
A long silence follows, then a soft laugh.
The gunfire grows closer, unmistakably so. Bullets seem to be tearing right past the receiver.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Have you secured your retreat?

items.speaker: Levchuk
items.text: Commander, I—Staff Sergeant Yaroslav Levchuk—have successfully completed my task.
Ptolemy pushes his way to the speaker.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: What are you saying? Goddammit! Don't you die on me! I'm coming to bring you back right now!

items.speaker: Levchuk
items.text: Stop causing trouble for the admiral, you hear, Ptolemy?
Artillery begins to drown out the staff sergeant's voice.

items.speaker: Levchuk
items.text: It has been a true honor serving under you, sir. I have no regrets.
*beep ... beep ... beep ...*
As the gunfire swells, the signal is cut off.
Along with the heavy breathing of their comrade.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Reorganize the troops, Ptolemy. All units save the anti-air squads are to evacuate from Bereggrad.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: Evacuate Bereggrad? To where? The safehouse?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: No, to the Cavalry Corps's sich.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: We will make Krutov return everything he stole from us.
The Gryphons bring the worst news.
The commander swallows his grief and feeds the casualty list to the coals.
In the solemn silence of the sich, he has already made his decision.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Tamarovka is the keystone of Krutov's plan.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: If it falls, Bereggrad will face a formidable arcanist force with armored vehicles. If only we had cut off their supply lines ...

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: The Legion can launch a raid from inside Tamarovka. They won't see it coming.

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: Even if your Gryphons could strike the enemy undetected ...
The chief of staff paces the length of the sand table for the third time.

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: They won't hold long if Krutov keeps getting supplies and reinforcements. We have to cut them off, but how?

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: I saw plenty of soldiers standing out by their horses. Couldn't they—

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: They're only kids!
Sternova slams her hands on the table, scattering the markers.

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: All the grown men rode out in the first sortie.

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: Most of them lied about their age, just trying to get a good meal. Their hands haven't even been toughened by the reins yet. They're boys! Not soldiers.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Sabina.
The commander pats her back and ushers her out of the tent.
The boys stand in their oversized uniforms, rifle straps digging into their thin shoulders, shashka scabbards dragging against their soft legs.
They stand quietly, their throats working under tight collars.
Their silence suppresses her anger.

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: Do you understand what you're facing?

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: In all likelihood, you'll die on the battlefield. You'll never see home again.

items.speaker: Teen Cavalryman I
items.text: Don't take me for a kid, ma'am! I'm a Cossack, like my brother, sister, and my parents before me!

items.speaker: Teen Cavalryman II
items.text: Ura! The blood of the Cossacks—of heroes—runs through me!

items.speaker: Teen Cavalryman I
items.text: We may be young, but our blood is strong. No Cossack fears the battlefield!

items.speaker: Teen Cavalryman I
items.text: If it means losing a hand, a leg, or even our lives, we'll do anything, make any sacrifice, to protect our homeland!
Those familiar words strike her deep.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: See, Igor?

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: These soldiers will drive those masked lunatics from the steppe.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Her future rests with the young. We old-timers have no right to shape this era.
The commander, eyes red, looks over these thin shadows.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Tell me, great riders of the steppe, will victory be ours today?

items.speaker: Teen Cavalryman I
items.text: Victory will be ours!

items.speaker: Teen Cavalryman II
items.text: We'll drive these madmen from our home!
Unbroken voices rise like the flow of the Don in spring, crashing into every corner of the sich.
The commander looks back, meeting the heavy gaze of the rebel leader.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Igor, this is our last chance.
His hands are noticeably quivering.
But no one blames him for it.
